messages:
maria: hey team — customer 'AcmeHealth' reporting failing streaming calls to private inference endpoint in their VPC. TLS handshake times out. they see SYNs go out from our egress IP 52.11.22.33 but no SYN-ACK coming back. can someone triage?
support-oncall: thanks maria — can you paste a tcpdump or packet snippet? also which endpoint IP + port and are they using NAT/GW?
maria: endpoint 10.2.5.18:443, calls originate from our fleet egress 52.11.22.33 (NAT EIP on their side). they said 'nat gateway' in their diagram. tcpdump attached (snippet):

--- tcpdump ---
52.11.22.33.49160 > 10.2.5.18.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0

(no reply lines for that flow)

support-oncall: OK that looks like reply dropped. two quick checks: 1) NACLs are stateless — you must allow both directions for ephemeral ports. 2) Security groups are stateful — if SG allows outbound 443 it's fine usually. ask customer to run: `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` on the host initiating the call and paste it.

kenji: +1 — also ask them to run `sudo tcpdump -n -i <if> host 10.2.5.18 and port 443` while reproducing. run `curl -v --resolve model.acme.internal:443:10.2.5.18 https://model.acme.internal/` and `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.5.18:443 -servername model.acme.internal -brief`. share outputs.

alex: quick theory: their NACL likely only permits inbound 443 (dest port 443) from our NAT EIP, but since NACLs are stateless the return packets from destination back to source ephemeral port must be allowed by the NACL inbound rule (destination port = ephemeral). If they only allowed 443 inbound and 1024-65535 outbound or similar mismatch you'll see exactly this behavior. NACL rules need matching ranges for both directions. Example recommended minimal NACL rules:

- allow 6 TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 (egress to model)
- allow 6 TCP 32768-65535 0.0.0.0/0 (ingress for reply)
- allow 6 TCP 32768-65535 0.0.0.0/0 (egress if they expect ephemeral-source on their side)

(remember AWS NACL is stateless — both directions required)

kenji: also check their NAT gateway behavior — NAT gateway may rewrite source port to a port outside the range they whitelisted. if they have an inline firewall before the instance it may be dropping replies. NAT can map source port into ephemeral range; so whitelisting only a narrow set can fail.

maria: they ran `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` -> "32768 60999". their NACL inbound only had a rule allowing port 443 and ephemeral outbound 32768-60999, inbound ephemeral missing.

support-oncall: yep that's the problem. ask them to add an inbound NACL allow for 32768-60999 (protocol TCP, source 0.0.0.0/0 or your NAT EIP range) with higher priority than the deny. then try again.

alex: extra debugging tips:
- `sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v` on their NAT/edge to see SNAT translations
- `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'host 52.11.22.33 and port 49160'` to verify replies reach the instance and see any RST/ICMP
- `traceroute -T -p 443 10.2.5.18` sometimes shows midbox dropping
- check ALB/NLB healthchecks and target-group port mapping if they front models with a LB

kenji: if they can't change NACLs quickly, temporary workarounds: 1) put our clients behind a proxy in same subnet (so no NAT rewrite) 2) use AWS PrivateLink/Interface endpoint for the model service 3) have customer open a narrower ephemeral range and ensure both rules present

maria: they applied inbound NACL 32768-60999 and now handshake completes. streaming resumed. thanks all. :thumbsup:

support_bot: incident 2026-03-15-2847654321 created and linked to ticket #INC-4821

alex: great — please capture the config (NACL rules + NAT translation sample) in the ticket and close when verified.

maria: will do, uploading screenshots and tcpdump to ticket now. closing thread when customer confirms for 24h stability. :white_check_mark:
